title: 1981-04-16_Pat_115.txt
concise_summary: PKD argues that VALIS, while appearing to be an existential novel addressing Heidegger's Dasein and verfallenheit, is actually structured backward as a Gnostic Gospel: he wrote from soteriological solution back to existential problem, grounding both in his direct 2-3-74 visionary experience of Jesus patibilis (the suffering form of primal man) interpreted through Manichaean-Gnostic categories. He develops a metaphysical model of two coaxial worlds (A and B) existing in 180-degree ontological opposition, unified by a hyperfield that permits simultaneous ignorance and gnosis, and demonstrates this duality through the Christian Fish sign and his novel Tears.
key_claims: VALIS fails as an existential work but succeeds as a Gnostic Gospel because it argues backward from soteriological solution to existential problem, not forward from problem to solution
The novel's internal coherence demands both the existential problem and the transmundane savior solution be accepted together or rejected together as indivisible
PKD's 2-3-74 vision was genuine and comprehensible within Manichaeism-Gnosticism specifically, revealing Jesus patibilis (suffering divine principle) not Christ returning in glory
Two mutually exclusive worlds (A: ostensible/official; B: covert/Gnostic truth) coexist coaxially with 180-degree sign-reversal through a hyperfield mechanism grounded in Platonic Forms (eide)
The hyperfield AB ontologically grounds the Gnostic categories of ignorance and knowledge as absolute rather than merely subjective perceptions
Certain objects serve in both worlds simultaneously (exemplified by the Christian Fish sign in 2-74), proving two worlds must coexist

tensions: PKD initially anticipated the orthodox Christian second advent but his 2-3-74 vision revealed Gnostic-Manichaean categories instead—a fundamental mismatch between expectation and experience

VALIS appears to be existential (addressing Heidegger, Dasein, verfallenheit) yet is actually Gnostic Gospel; this disguise may have been intentional or a reflection of PKD's own ignorance when writing

The sophisticated existentialist reader finds VALIS's soteriological solution insulting and absurd precisely because they understand the existential problem; thus the novel is most dangerous to those most capable of understanding its problem
PKD claims the hyperfield AB represents Platonic metaphysics (the Forms) yet simultaneously grounds Gnosticism—a tension between idealism and dualism that is not fully resolved
PKD acknowledges he does not fully know whether his later vision of Tagore was genuine or constructed ('saw' vs. saw), yet uses it to confirm the Manichaean system

The novel itself 'stops' and does not assert the truth of the soteriological solution, only reports what Fat believes; PKD excuses this by saying he knew nothing of Jesus patibilis when writing, yet he now claims perfect knowledge of it

PKD asserts both that the two worlds are absolutely ontologically opposed (180 degrees) and that they somehow coexist at one time and place, yet also at two times and two places 'in a lesser, merely seeming sense'—the logical mechanism remains elusive

The Cathare were destroyed in 1300 AD ('killing off'), yet Gnosticism/Manichaeism allegedly still operates covertly through the Plasmate manipulating media—tension between historical extinction and present operation
evidence_quotes: "The result would be absurd. The most critically Valis aspects of human existence would be juxtaposed with bizarre fantasy - +, worst of all, the latter would be introduced to solve the former - with the bitter result that the former (man's thrown + fallen Dasein) would seem just that much more hopeless."

"What he does not see is that 'Valis' is written backward, from solution (soteriology) to problem (verfallheit). The author is stipulating the problem only to account for the existence of the solution (he has reasoned back from the soteriological experience to the problem): he knows the solution firsthand + infers the problem using it as his premise."

"'Valis,' then, only seems to be an existential work; in reality it a Gnostic Gospel, + its main concern is with the perpetual transmundane savior who comes here (again + again) under a variety of names."

"Now I know that I saw primal man in his suffering form: Jesus patibilis; + that my soteriological confrontation was genuine + comprehensible within a given historical religious system (Manichaeism, which isn't even mentioned in 'Valis' simply because I could not spell it!)."

"This coincides with my theory of two information-systems competing: the plasmate cooking + riding our communications media is at 180° variance to the ostensible message-traffic. Thus all at once what seemed clearly to be Platonist metaphysics last February is still the case but it is how you get the two coaxial worlds."

"the novel itself... 'Tears' exists in both worlds + hence is part of hyperfield AB. It seems quite evident - even fundamentally obvious that not all things are. the whole thing is: certain (but not all) objects serve in both worlds, A and B. + this is what I caught the Xtian Fish sign doing in 2-74: one object seen twice; i.e. in both worlds whereupon I leaped to the obvious + ineluctable conclusion that if one object served both worlds, ipso facto there had to be two worlds."

"the goal of it all is: that your death should emanate out of what you are ontologically, + not part - the ultimate parts- of the Geworfenheit imposed on you as heimarmene, i.e. to which you succumb + must succumb this transformation occurs when you cease to run from your death, turn + face it + make it yours."
uncertainty_flags: OCR/transcription errors throughout: 'soteriological' sometimes rendered 'soterio logical', 'verfallheit' inconsistently spelled, 't C-185' and similar codes appear to indicate manuscript pages but their significance is unclear
Galbreath's identity and specific argument are cited but not fully detailed; unclear whether this is a published review, letter, or conversation
Reference to Kerygma (4:20 a.m. insight) is vague—unclear whether this refers to a written source or PKD's own visionary experience/dream
The exact nature of PKD's vision of Tagore six years after 2-3-74 (approximately 1980) is ambiguous: was it an actual vision or a reinterpretation of earlier experiences?
PKD's claim that he 'could not spell Manichaeism' when writing VALIS is somewhat confusing—whether he lacked the know-how or lacked knowledge of the system itself is unclear
The mechanism by which hyperfield AB concretely unites Platonist metaphysics with Gnostic dualism remains theoretically underdeveloped

PKD asserts that World A is both '(1) effortlessly seen' and '(2) not (somehow) the case' while World B is '(3) very difficult to see' and '(4) somehow is the case'—the logical coherence of something being simultaneously 'the case' and 'not the case' is not resolved

The reference to Jesus patibilis withdrawing and taking 'the entire spiritual principle' with him upon his ascent, leaving world to perish, echoes Manichaean theology but is not explicitly grounded in a canonical Manichaean source PKD cites
The claim that Fat's recovery is 'homologized with his anticipation of the imminent birth of the new savior' requires clearer definition of 'homologized' and its application to VALIS's narrative
